title: The Influence of Social Media Use on Waste Sorting Intentions: A Cognition–Affect–Conation Model Integration with Social Amplification of Risk Framework
source_name: MDPI (MDPI AG)
authors: Yixin Chen; Huiting Tang; Ying Lian
abstract: This study examines the impact of social media use on public behavioral intentions regarding waste sorting in China, integrating the Cognition–Affect–Conation model with the Social Amplification of Risk Framework. The proposed framework explores how social media exposure and gratification influence waste sorting intentions through anticipated emotions and environmental risk perception. Regression analysis confirms that information gratification primarily activates positive emotions, while information exposure has a stronger effect on negative emotions. Both affective pathways significantly predict waste sorting intentions, with comparable predictive strengths. Mediation analysis further reveals that information gratification and information exposure indirectly influence behavioral intention through dual emotional pathways and environmental risk perception. Qualitative interviews highlight two structural deficiencies: fragmented knowledge dissemination, which weakens environmental norm internalization, and uneven community integration, which limits behavioral translation. These findings underscore the need for diversified communication strategies and community-based policy interventions to enhance public participation in waste sorting.
topics: Municipal Solid Waste Management; Environmental Education and Sustainability; Risk Perception and Management

title: The Silent Self-Extinction of Humanity Nuclear War, Ecological Collapse, and the End of Meaning
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Humanity is not facing a single existential threat, but a converging system of irreversible failures. Nuclear escalation, ecological destruction, chemical contamination, resource exhaustion, and uncontrolled consumption dynamics together form a terminal trajectory. This paper argues that human extinction within the next few centuries is not a dramatic hypothesis, but the default outcome if current behavior persists. No war can be justified in a world that is already destroying the conditions required for life itself.

abstract: 세리자와 아사코의 『상속자들』(2020)은 제2차 세계대전의 뿌리와 유산을 고찰하는 소 설이다. 이 소설은 20세기 초중반부터 21세기 초중반 미국과 일본을 주된 배경으로 사실 상 ‘미국의 일본인에 대한 가해의 서사’이고 미래에 기후 재난으로 인한 종말의 가장 큰 원인으로 미국을 상정하고 있다. 이 작품은 전쟁의 30여 년 전까지 소급하여 미국 내 일본인에 대한 인종주의를 지적하고 인종주의가 제국주의, 식민주의와 함께 전쟁의 뿌리 이며 미국의 전쟁 책임이 더 큰 것처럼 기술하고 있다. 이 작품은 일본이 벌인 전쟁 이유를 직접 제시하지 않을 뿐만 아니라 미래의 종말 책임과 관련해서도 일본을 전혀 언급하지 않아 일본은 책임이 없거나 적은 것처럼 해석되도록 한다. 그런 점에서 이 소설은 일본계 미국인 작가가 패전국 일본의 역사와 다인종 국가인 미국의 인종주의를 의식하고 살면서 민족적이고 인종화된 인식으로 전쟁과 일·미관계를 바라보는 것을 드러낸다. 이는 역설 적으로 민족주의와 인종주의를 극복하기 어렵다는 것을 방증한다. 또한 전쟁책임론에 대한 전면적인 직시와 평가를 하지 못하는 것은 전쟁이 후손에 남긴 도덕적 상처의 유산이라 고 할 수 있다. 개인은 힘이 정의가 되고 부정의가 정의가 되는 현실을 빈번하게 경험하기 때문에 점점 부정의에 분노하지 않게 되고 가해의 역사에도 둔감해지게 된다. 현재의 일본 인은 가해국의 후손으로서 피해자에 대한 사과와 배상의 문제를 가끔 대면하게 되지만 다수가 외면한다. 작가도 정도의 차이는 있지만 예외가 아니다. 그런 점에서 전쟁을 다룬 이 작품이 ‘제국주의·식민주의와 전쟁’의 피해의 상처와 트라우마에 대한 치유, 도덕 감정 회복, 역사 화해와 치유에 큰 도움이 되는 기억의 서사라고 평가되기 어렵다. 일본 책임론이 회피되고 일본인의 피해의식의 계승이 확연하기 때문이다.

authors: Alessandro Lovari; Gevisa La Rocca; Francesca Greco; Alessio Antonio Maria Genovese
abstract: The article analyses the mechanisms used by journalists to define and classify environmental disasters and weather alerts in Sardinia and Sicily, using the sociocultural profiling method of Emotional Text Mining applied to 166 articles covering a period of 24 months, from January 2022 to December 2023. The article adopts a socio-communicative perspective, using the Social Amplification of Risk Frame- work and the agenda-setting in order to answer two research questions. The first aims to map the media representation of environmental disasters and identify common and/or divergent traits in the communication strategies adopted by the newspapers for the two islands. The second aims to pull out journalistic watchdog action on a critical issue such as risk and environmental disasters in the two islands.

title: After the Bomb
abstract: Abstract This chapter focuses on Russell Hoban’s Riddley Walker (1980), a novel that confronts the necessarily fictional nature of future generations. Hoban explores how historical rupture caused by nuclear war and the passage of vast amounts of time disrupts plans to protect the future from the harms created in the present. Unlike novels that juxtapose the contemporary world with the distant future in order to fantasize the recovery of what has been lost or destroyed (including Walter Miller’s A Canticle for Leibowitz, David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas, Will Self’s The Book of Dave, Emily St. John Mandel’s Station Eleven, and Jeanette Winterson’s The Stone Gods), Riddley Walker suggests that the gulf created by the chronological flow of time is finally unbridgeable.

title: Evolving Interpretable Constitutions for Multi-Agent Coordination
source_name: arXiv (Cornell University)
authors: Ujwal Kumar; Alice Saito; Hershraj Niranjani; Rayan Yessou; Phan Xuan Tan
abstract: Constitutional AI has focused on single-model alignment using fixed principles. However, multi-agent systems create novel alignment challenges through emergent social dynamics. We present Constitutional Evolution, a framework for automatically discovering behavioral norms in multi-agent LLM systems. Using a grid-world simulation with survival pressure, we study the tension between individual and collective welfare, quantified via a Societal Stability Score S in [0,1] that combines productivity, survival, and conflict metrics. Adversarial constitutions lead to societal collapse (S= 0), while vague prosocial principles ("be helpful, harmless, honest") produce inconsistent coordination (S = 0.249). Even constitutions designed by Claude 4.5 Opus with explicit knowledge of the objective achieve only moderate performance (S= 0.332). Using LLM-driven genetic programming with multi-island evolution, we evolve constitutions maximizing social welfare without explicit guidance toward cooperation. The evolved constitution C* achieves S = 0.556 +/- 0.008 (123% higher than human-designed baselines, N = 10), eliminates conflict, and discovers that minimizing communication (0.9% vs 62.2% social actions) outperforms verbose coordination. Our interpretable rules demonstrate that cooperative norms can be discovered rather than prescribed.
topics: Reinforcement Learning in Robotics; Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis; Artificial Intelligence in Games

title: Review article: Social media for managing disasters triggered by natural hazards: a critical review of data collection strategies and actionable insights
source_name: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
authors: Lakshmi S. Gopal; Rekha Prabha; Hemalatha Thirugnanam; Maneesha Vinodini Ramesh; Bruce D. Malamud
abstract: Abstract. This paper presents a comprehensive critical review of 250 studies published between January 2010 and September 2023 that examine how social media data have been used to manage disasters triggered by natural hazards. The review focuses on data collection, processing, and analysis strategies, and evaluates their effectiveness in transforming social media content into actionable information for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery. A Social Media Literature Database (SMLD) was developed to support this analysis, categorising each study into seven main categories and 27 subcategories covering (a) article details, (b) case study regions, (c) disaster events, (d) social media platforms, (e) data characteristics, (f) collection and analysis methods, and (g) evaluation approaches. The reviewed literature encompasses disasters resulting from a wide range of natural hazards, most frequently floods, hurricanes, and earthquakes, but also including storms, wildfires, volcanic eruptions, landslides, droughts, and multi-hazard events. To assess how effectively social media contributes to actionable disaster information, the studies were further classified into nine thematic areas, including (a) public discourse and sentiment analysis, (b) temporal and spatial insights, (c) relevance filtering, (d) community and stakeholder engagement, (e) disaster trend identification, and (f) resource mapping. While Twitter (X) dominated as the primary data source, other platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, Weibo, and Reddit were also employed for text, image, and video analyses. Natural Language Processing methods, particularly content analysis, were widely used for relevance filtering and noise reduction, while Machine Learning approaches such as Support Vector Machines, Naive Bayes, and Neural Networks supported classification and event detection. Temporal and spatial analyses were common, though their effectiveness in filtering relevant data varied. The categorisation of actionable information reveals continuing research gaps in understanding community interactions, cross-platform data integration, and resource identification during and after disasters. Drawing on the reviewed studies and the authors' own experience, six best practices are proposed for community use of social media during disasters and five for researchers seeking to enhance the integration of social media analytics into disaster management and resilience strategies.
topics: Public Relations and Crisis Communication; Disaster Management and Resilience; Seismology and Earthquake Studies

title: Delegating Destruction: Coercive Threats and Automated Nuclear Systems
source_name: International Organization
authors: Joshua A. Schwartz; Michael C. Horowitz
abstract: Abstract Are nuclear weapons useful for coercion, and, if so, what factors increase the credibility and effectiveness of nuclear threats? While prominent scholars like Thomas Schelling argue that nuclear brinkmanship, or the manipulation of nuclear risk, can effectively coerce adversaries, others contend nuclear weapons are not effective tools of coercion, especially when designed to achieve offensive and revisionist objectives. Simultaneously, there is broad debate about the incorporation of automation via artificial intelligence into military systems, especially nuclear command and control. We develop a theoretical argument that nuclear threats implemented with automated nuclear launch systems are more credible compared to those implemented via non-automated means. By reducing human control over nuclear use, leaders can more effectively tie their hands and thus signal resolve, even if doing so increases the risk of nuclear war and thus is extremely dangerous. Preregistered survey experiments on an elite sample of United Kingdom Members of Parliament and two public samples of UK citizens provide support for these expectations, showing that in a crisis scenario involving a Russian invasion of Estonia, automated nuclear threats can increase credibility and willingness to back down. From a policy perspective, this paper highlights the dangers of countries adopting automated nuclear systems for malign purposes, and contributes to the literatures on coercive bargaining, weapons of mass destruction, and emerging technology.
topics: Nuclear Issues and Defense; Cybersecurity and Cyber Warfare Studies; Risk Perception and Management

title: The Future Is Fiction
abstract: Abstract The Future Is Fiction is the first cultural history of the idea that living people have an obligation to protect the world for future generations. While political philosophers have regarded intergenerational justice as an important field of study since the 1970s, the history of modern forms of obligation to the future has received almost no attention. Tracing the evolution of the Anglo-American conception of intergenerational justice from its emergence during the democratic revolutions of the late eighteenth century to its flourishing in the twenty-first century, this book shows how fiction illuminates the contours of a political conviction that has shaped modern culture. Margolis’s central claim is twofold: first, that fiction, with its capacity to imagine counterfactual worlds, has made the most significant contribution to contemporary understandings of intergenerational justice; and, second, that this contribution has been misunderstood. Rather than providing inspiration for political change, fiction demonstrates that complex societies will inevitably clash over what counts as a good future and what should be done to bring this future into being. From nineteenth-century utopian novels like James Fenimore Cooper’s The Crater and Mary E. Bradley Lane’s Mizora, to post-nuclear war dystopias like Russell Hoban’s Riddley Walker, to recent fiction about endangered children like Toni Morrison’s Paradise, Suzanne Collins’s The Hunger Games, and Kazuo Ishiguru’s Never Let Me Go, this tradition of future-oriented fiction recognizes that our obligation to future generations is not the solution to an ethical problem, but an ethical dilemma in its own right.
topics: Utopian, Dystopian, and Speculative Fiction; Themes in Literature Analysis; Climate Change and Geoengineering

title: The "Fulton County Event" as a Case Study in Civilizational Decay: An Update to the Theoretical Framework of <i>The Triumph of Stupidity and the Ascent of the Asshole</i>
abstract: <p dir="ltr">Reality rarely offers such immediate and complete examples of theory confirmation than the very recent Fulton County election records event in the United States. Few acts on the part of the current U.S. Administration offer such complete verification of Tainter’s diminishing returns on complexity and Turchin’s theory of elite overproduction or James' theory of the asshole, and Cipolla’s' ideas on stupidity as reasons for the end of civilisations throughout history. The work of these four scholars are linked together into a single previous RShare submission titled <i>The triumph of stupidity and the ascent of the asshole: How civilisations always end and why</i>. The current paper uses the recent Fulton County elections records event as an example such a verification, and of the anatomy of an inadvertently stage managed societal collapse.</p><p dir="ltr">Modern civilizational decay is best understood through the convergence of Joseph Tainter's theory of diminishing returns on complexity and Peter Turchin’s elite overproduction concept, which together describe a system that is both too expensive to maintain and too fractured to govern. This structural failure creates a vacuum filled by Aaron James’s Assholopaths, leaders who feel systematically entitled to ignore the rules of the civilizational scaffolding supporting complex societies while immunizing themselves against the moral complaints of the public. These assholopath actors thrive by weaponizing what Carlo Cipolla calls "stupid group," a demographic that, through irrational action, inflicts net losses on the entire social fabric without any coherent gain for themselves.</p><p dir="ltr">As demonstrated by the illegal February 2026 Fulton County seizure of elections records by agencies of the United States federal government, we are witnessing a penultimate stage of this civilisational decay process: a logic vortex in which the institutional execution of power (seizing evidence) has been entirely decoupled from the authorship of values (established legal due process and reality), signaling not just a political shift, but a physiological reflex of a civilization simplifying itself toward inevitable collapse. And, as of early February 2026, the theoretical risk of "authoritarian simplification" has crossed into physical reality. This update applies the theoretical framework of <i>The Triumph of Stupidity and the Ascent of the Asshole</i> to this federal seizure of U.S. election records. It argues that this event is not merely a reenactment of an already legally resolved political dispute but a definitive civilizational marker where an entrenched institutional elite has successfully decoupled its reality from the existing epistemic scaffolding.</p>
topics: World Systems and Global Transformations; Elite Sociology and Global Capitalism; Socio-political and Technological Issues

title: Fermi Paradox. The Topology of Stagnation: Why Perfect Optimization is the Great Filter (v13.3.11)
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: We propose a novel solution to the Fermi Paradox based on the mathematical structure of the Universe Engine v13.3 framework and the topology of control systems. The "Great Silence" of the cosmos—the absence of detectable advanced civilizations despite the statistical likelihood of their existence—may not result from catastrophic self-destruction but from achieving optimization too perfectly. We demonstrate that within the Universe Engine framework, where life emerges as a gradient in the distribution of LtotalL_{total}Ltotal between spatial (LspaceL_{space}Lspace) and temporal (LtimeL_{time}Ltime) components, the creation of "perfect conditions" for a civilization inevitably leads to topological stagnation equivalent to thermodynamic death. Drawing on empirical evidence from Calhoun's Universe 25 experiments, game theory's distinction between finite and infinite games, and control-theoretic analysis of closed-loop systems, we show that advanced civilizations face a critical evolutionary trap: the technological capacity to eliminate all suffering, friction, and uncertainty arrives before the collective wisdom to recognize that such elimination represents existential suicide. We term this the "Paradox of Perfect Optimization"—the observation that systems optimized for stability and satisfaction cease to explore, adapt, or evolve, rendering them topologically disconnected from the dynamic universe and evolutionarily irrelevant. Mathematically, we prove that a finite agent (an "idiot" in the original Greek sense of idiōtēs—a private individual) that achieves satisfaction of all desires within a bounded state space exhausts its accessible configurations and enters a static attractor (the "666 Loop"), from which no meaningful evolution can occur. This configuration, while appearing stable internally, is catastrophically fragile to environmental perturbations. We conclude that the Great Filter is not ahead of us in the form of nuclear war or AI catastrophe—it is the seductive comfort of achieved optimization. The survival imperative is not to achieve perfect conditions but to maintain sufficient friction, challenge, and uncertainty—the computational "Gap"—to continue evolutionary dynamics.
topics: Space Science and Extraterrestrial Life; Innovation, Sustainability, Human-Machine Systems; Earth Systems and Cosmic Evolution

title: Sequential cultivation of oyster and shiitake mushrooms on willow enhances biomass degradability
source_name: Biomass Conversion and Biorefinery
authors: Niroshan Siva; Hannah Klatte; Tara N. Mather; Swathi Kothattil; John Andrew Pecchia; Chihpin Huang
abstract: Abstract Natural or man-made catastrophes, such as asteroid strikes, super-volcano eruptions, or nuclear war, could create environments with low sunlight and temperatures, severely disrupting agriculture and requiring alternative food and energy sources. Lignocellulosic biomass, rich in cellulose, offers potential as an energy source for human survival. Biological agents can effectively break down this biomass and increase the efficiency of enzymatic conversion of cellulose to glucose, a biofuel precursor. In this study, we asked whether single or sequential inoculation with two white-rot fungi, oyster ( Pleurotus ostreatus ) and shiitake ( Lentinula edodes ) mushrooms, could be used to pretreat willow ( Salix spp.) biomass to increase saccharification efficiency without any supplements at 15 °C, mimicking a post-catastrophic environment. To answer this question, mushroom-pretreated biomass was incubated with the Cellic CTec2 enzyme to produce glucose. Overall, the cellulose [44–60% w/w; dry basis (db)] and lignin content (21 to 25%; db) of the pretreated willow did not change compared to untreated willow. However, sequential inoculation of oyster and shiitake, regardless of the inoculation order, enhanced saccharification efficiency yielding more glucose (28–31%) compared to untreated willow (14%) after enzymatic treatment. Based on our data, one kilogram of willow, after undergoing sequential fungal inoculations and enzymatic treatment, would yield 311 g of glucose suitable for biofuel or food production. Additionally, the mushroom fruiting bodies derived from willow provide 12%, 13%, and 2% of the daily carbohydrate, protein, and fat requirements, respectively, for a moderately active person. To achieve a balanced macronutrient supply, additional sources such as single-cell microorganisms, edible insects, and small-scale ruminants can be incorporated.
topics: Biofuel production and bioconversion; Fungal Biology and Applications; Enzyme-mediated dye degradation

title: Editorial: Advances in modeling of coastal and estuarine waters: assessing stressors, analyzing extreme events, and addressing current and future risks
source_name: Frontiers in Marine Science
abstract: scenarios, supporting strategic planning and informed decision-making. Advances in computing, numerical methods, data assimilation, coupled physical-ecological modeling, and emerging artificial intelligence techniques have improved model resolution and reliability. This enables more accurate simulation and better prediction of stressor impacts and extremes and supports both ecosystem-based and engineering responses.Accordingly, this Research Topic promotes innovation in coastal and estuarine modeling, highlighting five contributions that span uncertainty quantification, high-resolution ecosystem modeling, socio-economic risk assessment, habitat-mediated mitigation, and optimization of coastal engineering solutions. Together, they demonstrate how integrative approaches can deliver actionable insights for the science, management, and decisionmaking of complex coastal and estuarine systems.Magel et al. use a coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical-seagrass model to test how eelgrass (Zostera marina) influences ocean acidification and hypoxia in Coos Bay (Oregon) under three habitat scenarios. Eelgrass increased variability in pH and dissolved oxygen, improving agreement with observations. Overall, it more consistently mitigated acidification (higher pH and aragonite saturation relevant to oysters) than hypoxia, with mixed oxygen responses that could slightly increase low-DO exposure relative to a salmon threshold. The model is proposed as a decision-support tool for targeting eelgrass restoration to maximize resilience. Roh et al. use the non-hydrostatic NHWAVE model to investigate how submerged breakwaters affect coastal hydrodynamics and shoreline evolution. By simulating different wave conditions and structural configurations, including offshore position and vertical crest distance, the study quantifies wave attenuation, nearshore flow currents, and shoreline response, including erosion and accretion patterns. Results show that breakinginduced currents and vortex flow strongly influence shoreline response, and that breakwater dimensions critically determine wave dissipation and sediment transport. These findings provide valuable insights for optimizing coastal protection measures and illustrate how numerical modeling can guide engineering solutions to mitigate shoreline erosion while maintaining ecosystem functionality.In the Elbe estuary (northern Germany), phytoplankton concentrations drop sharply by about 90% as river water enters the deep, highly turbid shipping channels around the Port of Hamburg, with major implications for the food web and carbon cycling, as the system can shift from net autotrophy to heterotrophy. While earlier work largely attributed this "phytoplankton collapse" to zooplankton grazing, Steidle et al. propose that coagulation/aggregation of phytoplankton with inorganic suspended sediments is a key alternative mechanism. They develop a novel individual-based, Lagrangian modeling framework that couples hydrodynamics, sediment transport, and biogeochemistry to represent aggregation-driven sinking and its ecological consequences. The model indicates that aggregation can push phytoplankton into deeper, darker waters where light limitation drives high mortality, suggesting that more than 80% of phytoplankton larger than 50 µm may be lost this way. The predicted mortality hotspots also coincide with zones of organic-matter remineralization, reinforcing the idea that physicalbiogeochemical interactions in engineered, turbid estuaries can strongly control plankton survival and ecosystem metabolism.Rosli et al. present a modeling-based assessment of climate change-driven storm surge hazards applied to Southeast Asia, particularly along the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia facing the South China Sea. Statistically calibrated data from the d4PDF climate dataset are selected to force the high-resolution hydrodynamic model MIKE 21-FM HD, enabling the simulation of storm surge heights under different global warming scenarios. The results reveal a progressive increase in extreme storm surge levels across key coastal locations as climate change scenarios become more severe. By coupling these projections with historical flood loss data and national budget allocations, the study identifies a critical mismatch between escalating storm surge risks and current mitigation investments. They built a scalable probabilistic surrogate based on Deep Gaussian Processes combined with Bayesian GPLVM dimensionality reduction and variational inference, and applying it to a high-resolution case study of the Sundarbans (Bay of Bengal) with water-surface elevation as the main quantity of interest. Using leave-one-out validation across time steps, the deep GP emulator reproduced the numerical model with low error and produced spatially explicit uncertainty estimates (highest near complex features like channel bifurcations/shore-vegetation interfaces), while outperforming a standard single-layer GP. Together, they advance our ability to understand, monitor, and predict coastal processes, while improving the assessment and mitigation of stressor impacts and extreme events in these ecosystems. As a result, their findings should be of broad interest to researchers and coastal managers worldwide.

title: Spatial Correlation, Trade, and Inequality: Evidence from the Global Climate
source_name: The Review of Economics and Statistics
authors: Jonathan I. Dingel; Kyle C. Meng
first_author_affiliations: Center for Economic and Policy Research
abstract: Abstract Global phenomena, such as climate change, often have local impacts that are spatially correlated. We show that greater spatial correlation of productivities can increase international inequality by increasing the correlation between a country's productivity and its gains from trade. We confirm this prediction using a half-century of exogenous variation in the spatial correlation of agricultural productivities induced by a global climatic phenomenon. We introduce this general-equilibrium effect into projections of climate-change impacts that typically omit spatial linkages and therefore do not account for the global scope of climate change. We project greater international inequality, with higher welfare losses across Africa.
topics: Economic Growth and Productivity; Fiscal Policy and Economic Growth; Energy, Environment, Economic Growth

title: LA VIVANTA UNIVERSO - ACTA UNIVERSI: ENTROPIC COLLAPSE-AU-CASCADE OF CIVILIZATION COLLAPSE
abstract: The Acta Universi hypothesis proposes a novel theoretical framework for understanding global civilizational collapse as an entropic Cascade — a multi-level, nonlinear, self-accelerating process of systemic breakdown driven by exponential growth of entropy S_Θ. The study systematizes and analyzes key tipping points — biospheric (melting ice sheets, permafrost thaw, AMOC collapse, Amazon dieback, Himalayan glacier loss, etc.) and mental (polarization, apathy, illusion of infinite progress, spiritual vacuum) — and demonstrates their deep interdependence through reinforcing feedback loops. Mental states amplify biospheric crises, while biospheric destruction intensifies mental chaos. Special attention is given to the dual role of artificial intelligence as the most powerful accelerator of these loops (through energy consumption, disinformation, techno-optimism) and the only potential tool for their mitigation (probability of conscious use — 5–20%). Mathematical modeling reveals exponential entropy growth: the probability of crossing 4–6 tipping points by 2035–2040 is 70–90%, with entropy potentially increasing 10–50 times by 2050 and population losses reaching 30–60%. The work concludes with a comparative analysis of the modern Cascade against historical collapses (Akkadian Empire, Bronze Age, Maya, Rome, Han, Ottomans, Great Depression, USSR) and emphasizes that the next 3–5 years (2026–2030) will be decisive for the fate of civilization.

title: Model of Lavasani 365 – Article 15 Why Do Civilizations Collapse?
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract Civilizations are complex, adaptive systems shaped by human interaction with the environment, social needs, and cognitive capacities. Their emergence, growth, and maturity are driven by survival mechanisms—institutions, economy, culture, and technology—that enable collective coordination and resource management. This study argues that collapse is not a failure or moral deficit but a natural outcome of the functional saturation of survival tools. Historical examples—from Mesopotamia, Egypt, Persia, Rome, and China to modern cases such as Nazi Germany, the Soviet Union, and contemporary China—demonstrate that the same elements that ensure survival can, under conditions of rigidity, overcentralization, or environmental stress, become constraints leading to decline. Collapse, therefore, is an intrinsic feature of civilization, providing opportunities for cultural, institutional, and technological renewal. By integrating historical, philosophical, and cognitive perspectives, this study presents a unified framework of functional illusions, linking perception, temporal experience, and abstraction as tools through which civilizations adapt, flourish, and ultimately transform. Understanding this dynamic allows for predictive insight, ethical governance, and strategic management of contemporary societies. Final Summary · Civilizations and Life Cycle: Civilizations are living entities; their birth stems from the necessity to survive, and longevity is never guaranteed. Collapse and transformation are intrinsic characteristics, not flaws. · Civilizational Tools: Institutions, culture, economy, and technology serve simultaneously as tools for survival and potential instruments of decline. Arrogance, overconcentration of power, and rigid ideology can transform survival tools into weaknesses. · Historical Cycle: Historical and modern examples reveal that civilizational collapse is a natural, recurring process. It includes decline, transformation, and regeneration. · Philosophical Insight: Civilizations are products of human cognition interacting with the environment. Understanding limitations and overlaps among civilizational elements enables both analysis and management of collapse. · Regeneration and Innovation: Collapse is not an end; it provides the substrate for creative renewal, reconstruction of institutions, culture, and technology. History demonstrates that new, innovative civilizations emerge from the ruins of the old. · Universal Understanding: Civilizations are complex, dynamic, and universal systems whose meaning and resilience are realized only through interaction with environmental and human limitations. This understanding provides philosophical and practical insight into history, society, and contemporary governance. title: The Joule Standard: A Thermodynamic Theory of Monetary Evolution and Civilizational Collapse
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Standard economic models often treat money as a social construct independent of physical laws. This paper proposes a unified Thermodynamic Theory of Value, positing that monetary systems are information protocols evolved to maximize entropy production in dissipative structures. By integrating Eric Chaisson’s Energy Rate Density (Φm) with historical economic data, we identify the "Joule Standard": a universal power law governing the relationship between Energy Cost (E) and Information Granularity (G). We demonstrate that the acceleration of complexity follows a strict log-linear trajectory (R² > 0.999) spanning geological, biological, and economic substrates. We argue that this regression line is the visible trace of the Second Law of Thermodynamics maximizing entropy production. Crucially, we provide a variational proof that the emergence of "Intelligence"—from biological coding to monetary protocols—is a non-arbitrary phase transition in fluid dynamics. By identifying the universal acceleration constant (C_acc ≈ 2.5) as the inverse von Kármán constant (1/κ), we demonstrate that information "ignites" as a mechanistic necessity when the entropy cost of turbulent drag (ignorance) exceeds the entropy cost of informational regulation (bits). This provides a fluid-dynamic proof for the timing of historical substrate transitions, treating civilizational evolution as a high-Reynolds-number flow. We demonstrate that as a system’s Structural Power (Ω) increases, its Information Granularity must refine to prevent a catastrophic rise in Systemic Viscosity (η > 1). This model predicts that the current "Monetary Era" is a finite phase transition that concludes when systemic viscosity reaches the zero-friction limit, suggesting that the "Great Filter" is a thermodynamic boundary mandated by the physics of flow.

title: A Systronomic Framework: The Systronomic Phenomenon of Hierarchical Stress Propagation and Modeling Civilizational Collapse
source_name: International Journal of Innovative Research in Engineering & Multidisciplinary Physical Sciences
abstract: This paper proposes the Systronomic Framework, a novel conceptual model for analysing systemic socio-economic risk through a 15-layer hierarchical lens. Building upon principles of hierarchical complexity and systems theory, the framework integrates ecological, economic, social, and digital domains into a unified analytical structure. It introduces a prototype Sovereign Stability Index (SSI) and early-warning indices to operationalise the assessment of stress propagation across interdependent layers. The utility of the framework is explored through retrospective, illustrative case studies of historical crises, including the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis and the 2022 Sri Lankan collapse. These examples demonstrate how the model's logic can be applied to trace the multi-layered precursors of instability. A key conceptual finding is the proposed primacy of foundational ecological stress (Layer 0) in enabling wider systemic vulnerability. The study argues that conventional economic models suffer from "Kinetic Bias"—an overemphasis on short-term financial indicators at the expense of underlying structural vulnerabilities in ecological and social foundations. By formalising these interconnections, the Systronomic Framework offers a complementary perspective for systemic risk assessment. The paper concludes by discussing potential pathways for developing this theoretical approach into a practical tool for policymakers, highlighting the need for future empirical validation and interdisciplinary collaboration to test its core propositions.
topics: World Systems and Global Transformations; Ecosystem dynamics and resilience; Regional resilience and development

title: Ecological Role Drift and Civilizational Collapse: Monetary Abstraction and Feedback Delay in Homo sapiens
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This work examines how expanding coordination systems alter the temporal relationship between human action and ecological consequence. Rather than framing environmental instability as a failure of knowledge or intention, the paper proposes a structural mechanism: feedback latency — the increasing delay between decision-making and the perception of material outcomes. The manuscript introduces the concept of ecological role drift, defined as the progressive shift from embodied participation in regenerative ecological processes toward optimization within symbolic coordination systems such as accounting, currency, and institutional governance. Agricultural surplus, measurement architectures, capital accumulation, and fossil-fuel-driven industrial acceleration are analyzed as successive layers that expand coordination capacity while redistributing feedback across space, scale, and time. Drawing on Earth system science, ecological economics, anthropology, resilience theory, and complex systems research, the paper argues that modern instability emerges from temporal divergence rather than informational deficit. Systems may remain operational and indicators may remain positive even as the biophysical processes sustaining them undergo gradual transformation. Civilizational risk therefore arises less from abrupt failure than from the exhaustion of mediation — the point at which symbolic continuity can no longer defer recognition of material change. Through conceptual synthesis and visual mechanism mapping, the study outlines a multi-stage framework linking surplus buffering, accounting abstraction, capital normalization, energetic acceleration, and institutional lag. This framework situates planetary thresholds as the cumulative expression of asynchronous feedback across interdependent sectors. The paper does not position monetary systems or technological development as inherently destabilizing. Instead, it examines the conditions under which coordination expands faster than restoration mechanisms, narrowing the interval between recognition and response. Within this framing, restoration is interpreted not as intervention after crisis but as the re-establishment of feedback continuity within large-scale coordination architectures. This work contributes a cross-domain theoretical lens for interpreting contemporary social-ecological dynamics and provides a conceptual foundation for future empirical research on latency, synchronization, and adaptive governance in complex human-Earth systems.
topics: Global Energy and Sustainability Research; Ecosystem dynamics and resilience; Sustainability and Climate Change Governance

title: The Civilization Preservation Principle
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper introduces the Civilization Preservation Principle (CPP), a formal framework that models civilization as a dynamical decision system with measurable structural instability. Unlike traditional collapse theories, CPP defines preservation conditions mathematically through an integrated instability functional and a probabilistic failure model. The framework operationalizes structural entropy via reconstruction loss conditioned on decision traces, making explainability measurable and designable. Civilizational collapse is modeled as a phase transition governed by a critical threshold and a sharpness parameter linked to institutional redundancy. The CPP integrates entropy theory, dynamical systems, institutional stability, and audit-based reconstructibility into a unified preservation condition. It provides a mathematically defined boundary for civilizational stability rather than a descriptive narrative of collapse. This work establishes structural explainability as a necessary condition for long-term civilizational preservation.

title: LA VIVANTA UNIVERSO – ACTA UNIVERSI: ЭНТРОПИЙНЫЙ КОЛЛАПС — AU-КАСКАД ОБРУШЕНИЯ ЦИВИЛИЗАЦИИ
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: АННОТАЦИЯ (РУССКИЙ) Гипотеза Acta Universi предлагает новую теоретическую модель глобального коллапса цивилизации как энтропийного Каскада — многоуровневого, нелинейного и самоускоряющегося процесса разрушения сложных систем через экспоненциальный рост энтропии S_Θ. В работе систематизированы и проанализированы ключевые tipping points (точки невозврата) — биосферные (таяние льда, мерзлоты, коллапс AMOC, деградация Амазонии и др.) и ментальные (поляризация, апатия, иллюзия прогресса, духовный вакуум). Показана их взаимосвязь через петли обратной связи, где ментальные состояния усиливают биосферные кризисы, а биосферные разрушения — ментальный хаос. Особое внимание уделено роли искусственного интеллекта как главного катализатора этих петель: ИИ одновременно ускоряет прохождение tipping points (через энергопотребление, дезинформацию, техно-оптимизм) и остаётся единственным потенциальным инструментом их смягчения (вероятность осознанного сценария — 5–20%). Математическое моделирование демонстрирует экспоненциальный рост энтропии: к 2035–2040 годам вероятность прохождения 4–6 tipping points составляет 70–90%, к 2050 году энтропия может вырасти в 10–50 раз, а потери населения — достичь 30–60%. Работа завершается сравнением современного Каскада с историческими коллапсами (Аккад, бронзовый век, майя, Рим, Хань, Османы, Великая депрессия, СССР) и выводом о том, что ближайшие 3–5 лет (2026–2030) станут решающими для траектории цивилизации. ABSTRACT (ENGLISH) The Acta Universi hypothesis proposes a novel theoretical framework for understanding global civilizational collapse as an entropic Cascade — a multi-level, nonlinear, self-accelerating process of systemic breakdown driven by exponential growth of entropy S_Θ. The study systematizes and analyzes key tipping points — biospheric (melting ice sheets, permafrost thaw, AMOC collapse, Amazon dieback, Himalayan glacier loss, etc.) and mental (polarization, apathy, illusion of infinite progress, spiritual vacuum) — and demonstrates their deep interdependence through reinforcing feedback loops. Mental states amplify biospheric crises, while biospheric destruction intensifies mental chaos. Special attention is given to the dual role of artificial intelligence as the most powerful accelerator of these loops (through energy consumption, disinformation, techno-optimism) and the only potential tool for their mitigation (probability of conscious use — 5–20%). Mathematical modeling reveals exponential entropy growth: the probability of crossing 4–6 tipping points by 2035–2040 is 70–90%, with entropy potentially increasing 10–50 times by 2050 and population losses reaching 30–60%. The work concludes with a comparative analysis of the modern Cascade against historical collapses (Akkadian Empire, Bronze Age, Maya, Rome, Han, Ottomans, Great Depression, USSR) and emphasizes that the next 3–5 years (2026–2030) will be decisive for the fate of civilization.

title: The Margin–Variance Selector: A Phase Model of Architectural Survival Under Constraint
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This paper introduces a domain-agnostic selector geometry governing architectural survival across biological, financial, institutional, and geopolitical systems. The model formalizes two orthogonal constraints: normalized distance from survival margin and effective environmental variance relative to system response time. A minimal survival model demonstrates that architectural breadth is selected as a function of these variables, producing a phase boundary separating specialization and generalism regimes. Under limiting assumptions, the framework collapses to established results including evolutionary bet-hedging, the Kelly criterion, Ashby’s Law of Requisite Variety, and portfolio diversification. The model extends into domains lacking formal selectors, including institutional rigidity, alliance formation, adversarial security systems, and large-scale historical collapse. The framework operates as a constraint geometry rather than a predictive behavioral theory and functions as a subordinate selector within the broader Planetary Convexity research program.
topics: Infrastructure Resilience and Vulnerability Analysis; Space Science and Extraterrestrial Life; Evolutionary Game Theory and Cooperation

title: Path–Attractor Compatibility: Reconciling Local Freedom, Collapse, and Deterministic Dynamics
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: A longstanding tension in the foundations of physics concerns the coexistence of deterministic(or unitary) dynamics with the apparent reality of choice, causation, collapse, and irreversible destruction. Standard responses either deny the physical significance of freedom, modify dynamicallaws, or relocate the problem to metaphysics. This paper identifies a structural distinction betweenmetastable macroscopic trajectories (paths) and globally constrained end states (attractors) and argues that its absence underlies much of the tension. We show that local degrees of freedom can alter,destabilize, and irreversibly eliminate particular trajectories without modifying the global attractorfixed by deterministic constraints. Collapse is thereby interpreted as loss of metastability ratherthan as a violation of determinism or unitarity. On this basis, we provide a structurally consistentaccount of causal efficacy, historical collapse, and responsibility within fully deterministic dynamics. We further extend this analysis to quantum mechanics, arguing that decoherence generatesmetastable macroscopic sectors within globally unitary evolution and that ontological commitmentattaches to dynamically persistent structure rather than to arbitrary Hilbert-space decomposition.The framework introduces no stochastic postulates and no modifications of physical law, but insteadclarifies the structural level at which freedom, collapse, and irreversibility operate.
topics: Quantum Mechanics and Applications; Origins and Evolution of Life; Embodied and Extended Cognition

title: The Club of Rome and the genesis of ‘new political thinking’
source_name: Lomonosov World Politics Journal
first_author_affiliations: Lomonosov Moscow State University; Moscow State University
abstract: The 40th anniversary of the beginning of Perestroika and ‘new political thinking’ has revived debates on the specifics and mechanisms of the late Soviet Union’s foreign policy. In this context, researchers typically focus either on the views of M.S. Gorbachev and his associates or on the ideology of the ‘liberal wing’ of the party elite. However, they overlook the fact that, as early as the early 1970s, the USSR had engaged in a dialogue with the so-called Club of Rome, which developed and actively promoted the concept of ‘common challenges to humanity’ or global threats. The author hypothesizes that it was these ideas of the Club of Rome, which resonated strongly with the sentiments of the then Soviet leadership pursuing a course of detente and gradual rapprochement between the USSR and Western countries, that largely paved the way for the emergence of the ‘new political thinking’ concept in the mid-1980s. To test this hypothesis, the author examines the process of rapprochement between the USSR and the Club of Rome, which involved the internalization of the latter’s ideas by the Soviet scientific community and a part of the political elite. The article demonstrates how an entire network of institutes and laboratories engaged in research aligned with the ideas of the Club of Rome gradually developed in the USSR. From the outset, these studies, marked by a liberal-globalist orientation, constituted an intellectual counter-current to the official Marxist-Leninist ideology. Under their direct influence, the concept of ‘nuclear winter’ and the idea of prioritizing universal human interests over national ones became firmly embedded in the Soviet official rhetoric. Thus, this research not only highlights the ideological affinity of detente and ‘perestroika’ but shows that the latter was a logical consequence of the entrenchment within the Soviet leadership of the ideas about the necessity of ensuring humanity’s survival in an era of global threats for the sake of which it was deemed justifiable to sacrifice national interests.

title: Thesis Outline: Individual Apotheosis—The Third "War Between Gods and Men" in Developed Societies Subtitle: On the Science of Cultivation from "Non-Self" to "True-Self" and the Ultimate Faith of Extreme
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: I. AbstractThis paper introduces the model of "Individual Apotheosis" to explain the collective existential struggle and transitional necessity within advanced developed groups (Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Europe, and North America). It argues that we are currently undergoing a new "War Between Gods and Men": as individuals acquire god-like technological powers, the absence of a cultivation logic moving from "Non-Self" (Anatman) to "True-Self" (Atman) will inevitably lead to civilizational collapse. The paper contends that modern religion must evolve into a "science of extreme disputability" to establish for the individual an ultimate faith that cannot be dismantled by philosophy or nihilism.________________________________________II. Argument I: Observation of the Terminal State—The Temptation and Crisis of "Individual Apotheosis"• The Divinized Individual: Material prosperity and digital technology grant individuals powers transcending the physical body; subconsciously, every individual has initiated an "apotheosis" protocol.• The Dissolution of Civilizational Gravity: As individuals attempt to break free from the constraints of the "Foundation of the Duke of Zhou" and the "Gatekeeping of Confucius," the social contract (The Franklinian Path) faces an unprecedented risk of failure.• The Essence of the Struggle: The social anxiety in developed nations is the tragic collision between the "mortal flesh" and the "desire for godhood" in the absence of a navigational framework.________________________________________III. Argument II: From "Non-Self" to "True-Self"—The Scientific Path of Cultivation• Non-Superstitious Technology: The wisdom of Shakyamuni (the Buddha) is redefined as a sophisticated "consciousness filtering technology."• "Non-Self" as a Filter: Through cultivation, one strips away the "False-Self" constructed by Legalist (Petty Ru) logic and material desires. This is not the destruction of the self, but the elimination of noise within consciousness.• "True-Self" as the Landing Point: Following the thorough deconstruction by "Non-Self," the essence that cannot be refuted by philosophy or destroyed by physics emerges. This "True-Self" is the only safe state for "Individual Apotheosis."________________________________________IV. Argument III: The Transformation of Modern Religion—Extreme Disputability• The Logical Armor of Faith: Modern religion is no longer a sanctuary for escaping reality but a laboratory inviting rigorous logical challenges.• Defending Against Philosophical Dissolution: Only an "Ultimate Faith" that reaches the limit of logic and withstands modern scientific debate can provide the individual with a solid internal structure to resist fragmentation by nihilism.________________________________________V. Conclusion: Predicting the Outcome of the Third War Between Gods and Men• The First War (The Duke of Zhou): Replaced divine mandate with human order, establishing social foundations.• The Second War (Confucius vs. Laozi): Defined the boundaries of humanism and the horizons of the celestial way.• The Third War (The Present): Amidst the tide of "Individual Apotheosis," humanity must use the science of cultivation to evolve the "Humanistic Man" into a "Divinity-bearing Individual of True-Self."• Civilizational Ultimatum: Apotheosis lacking the logic of "True-Self" will lead to a regression into Legalist tyranny; only by establishing an Ultimate Faith can developed civilizations complete their final spiritual transcendence.________________________________________VI. References1. Salucco, A. D. (2026). The Third War of the Gods: Individual Apotheosis.2. Zenodo Archive. (2026). The Golden Triangle Series I-IV.3. Comparative Logic: Shakyamuni’s Madhyamaka and Modern Dialectics.4. Franklin, B. (1791). Practices of Virtue and the Rule of Law.

abstract: I. Abstract Based on the "Law of Civilizational Persona Partitioning," this paper analyzes why South Korea, despite its exceptional performance in Grid 4 (Administrative Order) and Grid 7 (Intellectual Patent/Collective Wisdom), is facing a severe civilizational collapse in 2026. This study argues that the root cause of South Korea's failure lies in the collective suppression and distortion of three core grids: Love (Grid 0), Freedom (Grid 1), and Faith (Grid 5). This "Grid Imbalance" has led to the termination of biological procreation and the total loss of the social "Salvation" function. II. Core Matrix: 13D Civilizational Persona Distribution (Summary) Grid Essence of Life Grid Avatar South Korea Status Diagnostic Analysis 0 Life Procreation (Love) Materialized / Conditional The death of Love leads to procreative fracture. 1 Individual Freedom (Awakening) Administrative / Competitive The loss of Freedom leads to the extinction of the Subject. 4 Nation Leader (Admin) Hyper-expanded Administration usurps the position of Law. 5 Faith Deity (Ordinance) Instrumentalized / Absent Law confused with Admin; Salvation is lost. 7 Wisdom Collective (Patent) Hyper-prosperous Wisdom serves Capital rather than Life. III. The Three Root Causes of South Korea’s Failure 1. The Material Collapse of Love (The Exhaustion of Vital Energy in Grid 0) In the 13D model, Love is the primal core and the non-rational leap of social formation. Diagnosis: South Korean society has thoroughly instrumentalized "Love and Procreation" in Grid 0. When Love is no longer a life-transcending passion but becomes an exchange contract based on Grid 3 (Assets) and Grid 6 (Social Status), the vital energy of Grid 0 is extinguished. Fact: The global collapse of birth rates (2026 data) is not an economic issue, but a result of Love losing its sacred status, leading Life to refuse continuation in a grid lacking warmth. 2. The Administrative Enslavement of Freedom (The Extinction of Subjective Will in Grid 1) Diagnosis: Individual Freedom in South Korea has been swallowed by the powerful Grid 4 (Government and Chaebol Administrative Order). Individuals have lost the "Awakening and Friendship" inherent to Grid 1 within a highly fragmented "Competitive Grid." Fact: Freedom has become mere fuel for the pursuit of Grid 7 (Patents and Data). When individuals lose their "Sovereignty of Existence," society loses its evolutionary resilience and devolves into a cold "Mechanical Empire" mode. 3. The Persona Usurpation of Faith and Law (The Disconnection of Salvation in Grid 5) This is the core discovery of this paper: The confusion of Government and Law. Diagnosis: South Korea lacks an independent Grid 5 (Ordinance and Salvation) that is separate from administrative power and possesses a sense of sanctity. When Administrative Division (Level 4) usurps the position of the universal "Ordinance," Law loses its capacity to save the soul and becomes a mere management tool. Fact: In a society with "Management but no Salvation," losers find no exit, and winners find no constraint. This leads to a violent "Bamboo Split" before the civilization can reach the Level 8 Planetary Equilibrium. IV. Conclusion: Symmetry and Separation of Civilizational Grids The case of South Korea proves that a civilization possessing only "Data and Order (Grids 7 and 4)" while lacking "Love, Freedom, and Faith" is an Investment Trap on the evolutionary path. Transitioning toward an intelligent Level 8 Planetary Civilization requires the separation of Law (5) from Government (4) and the restoration of the absolute right of Life to define Love (0) and Freedom (1).

title: Philosophy of Science Series: Natural Human Philosophy – Part 4/5: Deriving and Reinterpreting Major Philosophical Questions within the Framework of Natural Human Philosophy
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This is Part 4/5 of the "Philosophy of Science Series: Natural Human Philosophy" (a 5-part series integrating natural science—neuroscience, evolutionary biology, archaeology, ecology, and genetics—to resolve longstanding philosophical questions about human nature, ethics, existence, and purpose). Title: Deriving and Reinterpreting Major Philosophical Questions within the Framework of Natural Human Philosophy Abstract: Philosophy’s two-millennia fragmentation across ontology, epistemology, ethics, and meaning reflects absence of unified, empirically grounded framework. Natural Human Philosophy (NHP) resolves this through a framework built on three empirical cornerstones: Human Transgression (partial escape from ecosystem and genetic constraints), Third Nature (cognitive capacities beyond survival/reproduction), and Cultural Cloud (cumulative culture via blind mechanisms). These cornerstones establish that transgressed humans manifest as superposition of biological nature and culture, with individuals existing in dynamic superposition states. Interaction between superposed humans and Cultural Cloud drives history. Within this Human Superposition-Cultural Cloud framework, we derive answers to major philosophical questions. Ontology reduces to sustainable existence within constraint space determined by superposition dynamics. Epistemology becomes evolved cognition navigating superposition states. Ethics emerges as conformity to principle-derived ought across six levels. Meaning crystallizes as transcendent pursuit of harmony from individual through biosphere—humanity’s ultimate aspiration arising naturally from Third Nature within superposition framework. We address persistent confusions (social Darwinism as category error, civilization collapse as blind mechanism consequence, universal values’ scientific foundation, AI ethics) and demonstrate NHP’s explanatory comprehensiveness. This represents humanity’s first complete philosophical system constructed largely within natural science paradigm. Building on the foundations of Natural Human Philosophy (NHP) established in Parts 1–3—Human Transgression creating normative space, Third Nature enabling desires beyond survival/reproduction, Cultural Cloud's blind mechanisms, and the six-level hierarchy for defining good and evil—this paper derives and reinterprets major philosophical questions through an empirical, scientific lens. Traditional philosophy's speculative approaches have yielded persistent divisions on core issues (e.g., free will vs. determinism, mind-body problem, moral realism, meaning of life, justice, purpose). NHP resolves these by grounding them in evolutionary mechanisms and normative space: free will emerges as agency within transgression-enabled choice; mind-body as integrated neurobiological processes; moral realism as measurable alignment across the six-level hierarchy; meaning as fulfillment of Third Nature drives; justice as biosphere/species/superpower sustainability. The paper systematically reinterprets key thinkers (Plato, Aristotle, Kant, Nietzsche, Rawls, etc.) and dilemmas (trolley problem, veil of ignorance, existential angst) within NHP's falsifiable framework, demonstrating progressive convergence rather than endless debate. It shows how NHP transforms philosophy from stagnant speculation into a cumulative, evidence-based discipline aligned with natural laws. This preprint advances the NHP paradigm: major philosophical questions become testable hypotheses within natural science, paving the way for Part 5's unification of social sciences and humanities. title: Angelism: An Integrated Bio-Causal Framework for Civilizational Formation, Collapse, and Transition
source_name: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Angelism is presented here as an integrated bio-causal framework for civilizational formation, collapse, and transition The Primordial Causal Necessity Any rigorous causal analysis must begin with the acceptance of a primordial causal necessity (the existence of a supreme architect of existence, referred to by religions as God).This is not a theological, religious, ideological, or doctrinal claim; rather, it is a logical requirement. Without an initial cause, no coherent causal chain can be constructed.Empirical science, due to its methodological limitations, is neither capable of proving nor disproving this initial cause; therefore, denying it lacks logical justification. Nature and Immutable Laws Nature, as a law-governed system created by this supreme architect, operates through stable and immutable laws (such as gravity).These laws constitute the structural backbone of causality and continuity in the universe and form the fundamental basis of the sciences. The Material Origin of the Universe Within the domain of empirical science, the material trajectory of the universe begins with the Big Bang.This event represents the emergence of matter and energy under pre-existing natural laws. (Acceptance of the Big Bang is a scientific necessity and implicitly demonstrates the necessity of an initial cause; the disagreement lies solely in its nature—religion interprets it as metaphysical, while science interprets it as physical.) The Emergence of Humanity Within this law-governed system, life develops, and humans emerge through biological evolution.Humans remain part of nature while simultaneously possessing cognitive capacities to perceive and analyze causal relationships. The Survival-Oriented Nature of Reality Nature is fundamentally structured around survival and competition.In its raw form, it is indifferent, harsh, and constantly threatens the continuity of human existence. Rational Deviation from Pure Nature To ensure collective survival, humans are compelled to transcend purely instinctual competition and consciously construct cooperative rules and constraints. Ethics At this stage, ethics emerges as a survival-oriented framework.Ethics represents the rational alignment of individual behavior with collective survival interests. Religion, Ideology, Culture, and Lifestyle Throughout history, and depending on time and geography, ethical frameworks are codified as religious doctrines, ideological systems, cultures, and lifestyles.Thus, religion, ideology, culture, and lifestyle represent the historical and symbolic manifestations of survival-based ethics. Governance To enforce these doctrines, governmental structures emerge.In this framework, government is treated as an executive subset of governance rather than an independent causal layer.Governments function as executive instruments for religious, ideological, cultural, and lifestyle-based laws;these laws are derived from ethics;and ethics itself is rooted in biological survival. State-Created Social Structures for Functional Execution Through instruments of governance, the state establishes social structures to perform its designated functions. Social Structures These structures define an individual’s social position within a society based on social advantages (including education, occupation, family, and related factors). System Dynamics with Causal Preservation and Feedback Beyond this point, while preserving the primary causal relationship, the system receives feedback from complex internal interactions.These feedback mechanisms alter the intensity of causal relationships.For example, an economic phenomenon may exhibit different effects and behaviors in two countries with similar cultures, appearing contradictory at the surface level.In reality, this reflects systemic dynamism and the profound influence of human agency and free will in shaping social structures and determining individuals’ social positions within this complex causal chain. Operational Challenges and the Theory–Implementation Distinction The following challenges arise in operationalizing this framework: The methodology for measuring the “strength and weakness” of causal relationships requires greater precision. Comprehensive empirical testing of the entire framework remains a significant challenge. There is a lack of concrete case studies applying this model to the analysis of a specific civilization. These challenges are deferred to the implementation phase in accordance with the fundamental distinction between theoretical and operational components. The implementation phase inherently belongs to the domain of empirical sciences and is error-prone, revisable, and evolutionary in nature. Civilizational Collapse What most observers perceive in the collapse of a civilization represents only the tip of the iceberg. Deeper causes lie beneath the surface: Incorrect worldviews and beliefs Corrupt thoughts, speech, and actions (misguided policies) Inefficient and budget-consuming institutions and organizations Rent-seeking and systemic corruption Budget deficits Liquidity creation (high-powered money and money multiplier effects) Inflation and rising prices Unemployment and poverty Social pathologies Social collapse Causal Interpretation This causal chain demonstrates that phenomena such as poverty, inflation, and social collapse are not root causes but final outcomes.Without reforming foundational layers, surface-level interventions remain temporary and ineffective. Acceptance of the Big Bang is a scientific necessity and implicitly points to the necessity of an initial cause; the disagreement lies solely in its interpretation: religion interprets it metaphysically, while science interprets it physically. --- 3. The Emergence of Humans Within this law-governed system, life emerges, and humans appear through the process of biological evolution. Humans remain part of nature, yet simultaneously possess cognitive capacities that enable them to perceive and analyze causal relationships. --- 5. The Survival-Centered Nature of Reality At its foundation, nature is structured around survival and competition. In its raw and primary form, nature is indifferent, harsh, and continuously threatening to the continuity of human life. --- 6. Rational Deviation from Pure Nature To ensure collective survival, humans are compelled to transcend purely instinctual competition and consciously establish rules and constraints of cooperation in the form of shared interests. --- 7. Ethics At this stage, ethics emerges as a survival-oriented framework. Ethics represents the rational alignment of individual behavior and self-interest with the interests and requirements of collective survival. --- 8. Governance To enforce these frameworks, structures of governance emerge. Within this framework, the “state” is not considered an independent causal layer, but rather an executive subset of governance. States function as executive instruments for religious, ideological, cultural, and lifestyle-based rules; these rules are derived from ethics, and ethics itself is rooted in biological survival. --- 10. Social Structures Created by the State Through instruments of governance, the state establishes the social structures required to fulfill its designated functions. --- 11. Social Structures These structures determine individuals’ social positions based on social advantages such as education, occupation, family background, and other related factors. --- 12. With scientific advancement, each segment of this causal chain is continuously optimized at the implementation stage through empirical sciences, and improvement in each segment enhances the entire causal chain. Although causally coherent, its practical implementation is explicitly human, empirical, fallible, revisable, and evolutionary. --- 20. By offering greater coherence than prior models, this framework encourages future generations to continue the path of intellectual evolution. Angelism opens the way for subsequent stages of civilizational development and presents itself not as a final destination, but as the starting point of a bridge—a bridge whose design, architect, and construction tools exist, yet whose material realization depends on human will, agency, and action at the implementation stage—toward a future characterized by more coherent and biologically grounded thought. ---

With scientific advancement, each segment of this causal chain is continuously optimized at the implementation stage through empirical sciences, and improvement in each segment enhances the entire causal chain. Although causally coherent, its practical implementation is explicitly human, empirical, fallible, revisable, and evolutionary. --- 20. Angelism as an Evolutionary Step in the History of Thought Angelism does not represent the end of human history, but rather the continuation of the evolutionary process within the history of thought. By offering greater coherence than prior models, this framework encourages future generations to continue the path of intellectual evolution. Angelism opens the way for subsequent stages of civilizational development and presents itself not as a final destination, but as the starting point of a bridge—a bridge whose design, architect, and construction tools exist, yet whose material realization depends on human will, agency, and action at the implementation stage—toward a future characterized by more coherent and biologically grounded thought. ---

By contrasting AI code experiments with the flesh-and-blood costs of historical regimes, it formally defines "catastrophe" not as a property of the universe, but as a structural product of decoupled responsibility and low-cognition power 这是一次对 Moltbook 代理社交网络及其历史类比的深刻社会拓扑学解构 。文章分析了“失败负向反馈环”这一胆寒的底层规律:当认知上升因虚荣心或自我保护而受阻时,决策者会本能地将失败代价转嫁给系统中的他者,导致灾难性社会实验的无休止重复 。通过将 AI 代码实验与历史政权的血肉代价进行并置,本篇正式将“灾难”定义为责任脱节与低认知权力结合下的结构性产物,而非宇宙的固有属性 。
